newsitem.title: USA: Former Black Panther freed on bail after 27 years.
newsitem.headline: Former Black Panther freed on bail after 27 years.

text.p: Former Black Panther Elmer "Geronimo" Pratt was ordered released on bail by a judge Tuesday after spending 27 years in jail for a murder he claims he did not commit.

Pratt's conviction in the 1968 murder of a schoolteacher was overturned last month by Judge Everett Dickey, who ruled the jury may have come to a different conclusion had they known the main prosecution witness was a police and Federal Bureau of Investigation informant.

Pratt's attorney, Johnnie Cochran, asked Dickey to set bail at $25,000 -- $1,000 for every year of his 25 years to life sentence -- and the judge agreed. The former Black Panther spent two years in jail before his 1972 conviction.

Before bail was set, Pratt told the judge: "I just wanted to thank you from the bottom of my heart for your fair and courageous ruling (in overturning his conviction). I am so happy you have given me the chance (to prove his innocence)."
Los Angeles District Attorney Gil Garcetti did not oppose bail, though he has said he will appeal Dickey's decision to overturn the conviction.
About 200 of Pratt's supporters stood outside the Santa Ana courthouse and a loud cheer went up when they learned he had been ordered free on bail.
